bibl.title: Architecture and organization of mouse posterior parietal cortex relative to extrastriate areas

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: The two major aims of this study were therefore (i) to provide a resource for identifying mouse PPC with anatomical criteria that are evident using ubiquitous staining methods, such as a Nissl stain, and (ii) to define where PPC falls in relation to extrastriate areas around V1.

span.label: mouse posterior parietal cortex delineation and connectivity
span.quote: Although recent years have seen a considerable rise in the use of rodents, particularly mice, to investigate PPC and related networks, a coherent anatomical definition of PPC in the mouse is still lacking.

span.label: anatomical-tract-tracing
span.term: anatomical-tract-tracing
span.quote: Additionally, we performed bilateral triple anterograde tracer injections in primary visual cortex (V1) and prepared flattened tangential sections from one hemisphere and coronal sections from the other, allowing us to co-register the cytoarchitectural features of PPC with V1 projections.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A WIDELY USED REGION NAME IS REPORTED TO HAVE NO COHERENT DEFINITION, AND THE COST IS NAMED: despite the popularity of the animal for studying the region there is LITTLE CONSENSUS ON A COHERENT ANATOMICAL DEFINITION, WHICH IS PROBLEMATIC BECAUSE IT COMPLICATES THE INTERPRETATION OF THE WEALTH OF NEW DATA. The missing definition is treated as a defect in the literature's ability to read its own results
span.quote: Despite the popularity of the mouse for studying parietal cortex, however, there is little consensus on a coherent anatomical definition of PPC in the mouse, which is problematic because it complicates the interpretation of the wealth of new data.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE PARTS THAT ARE ILL-DEFINED ARE ENUMERATED RATHER THAN GESTURED AT: what remains ILL-DEFINED is named as the BOUNDARIES which distinguish it from neighbouring areas, its LAMINAR ORGANIZATION and its CHEMOARCHITECTURAL PROFILE - three specific things, each of which a definition would have to fix
span.quote: More detailed aspects of mouse PPC anatomy, including the boundaries which distinguish it from neighboring areas, its laminar organization and chemoarchitectural profile remain ill-defined.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: IN THE ABSENCE OF A DEFINITION, PRACTICE SUBSTITUTES TWO PROXIES, AND BOTH ARE NAMED: targeting has relied EITHER on functional mapping of the areas around the region OR on stereotactic coordinates followed by POST-HOC HISTOLOGICAL COMPARISON to one of SEVERAL REFERENCE ATLASES. Where the definition is missing, the coordinates and the atlas stand in for it
span.quote: Recent strategies for targeting PPC in mice have therefore relied either on functional mapping of extrastriate areas around PPC (Wang & Burkhalter, 2007), or on stereotactic coordinates followed by post-hoc histological comparison to one of several reference atlases

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AND THE PROXIES ARE CONSISTENT WITHIN A STUDY AND INCOMPARABLE ACROSS STUDIES, FOR A STATED REASON: these conventions MAY YIELD CONSISTENT RECORDING LOCATIONS WITHIN A STUDY, BUT HAMPER THE COMPARISON of the region ACROSS STUDIES, SINCE THEY ARE BASED ON DIFFERENT LABELING METHODOLOGIES AND UNRELATED NOMENCLATURES. Reliability inside a lab and incommensurability between labs, traced to the naming systems themselves
span.quote: These conventions may yield consistent recording locations within a study, but hamper the comparison of PPC across studies since they are based on different labeling methodologies and unrelated nomenclatures.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE CONTRIBUTION IS EXPLICITLY A RECONCILIATION OF NOMENCLATURES, NOT A NEW FINDING: the paper states that it RECONCILED WIDELY USED BUT DISPARATE NOMENCLATURES referring to the region VERSUS the areas around it - two naming systems, each with its own literature, mapped onto one another
span.quote: Importantly, we reconciled widely used but disparate nomenclatures that refer to PPC (Paxinos & Franklin, 2012) versus the extrastriate areas around it

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE NEW DEFINITION IS ASSEMBLED FROM FOUR INDEPENDENT KINDS OF EVIDENCE, AND THE LIST IS THE DEFINITION: the combined approaches are said to provide A COHERENT DEFINITION that INCORPORATES laminar architecture, extrastriate projections, thalamic connections and cortico-cortical connections. Nothing here is a criterion on its own; the definition is the conjunction
span.quote: These combined approaches provide a coherent definition of mouse PPC that incorporates laminar architecture, extrastriate projections, thalamic, and cortico-cortical connections.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE DEFINING CRITERIA ARE STAINS - THE DEFINITION IS OPERATIONALISED BY REAGENTS: the region is delineated using CYTOARCHITECTURAL AND LAMINAR CRITERIA obtained from Nissl-, parvalbumin- and type-2 muscarinic acetylcholine receptor-immunostained sections. What the term picks out is fixed by what three stains show
span.quote: We sought to resolve these discrepancies by first delineating mouse PPC using cytoarchitectural and laminar criteria obtained from Nissl-, parvalbumin (PV)-, and type-2 muscarinic acetylcholine receptor (M2AChR)-immunostained coronal sections.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AND ONE STATED AIM IS THAT THE CRITERIA BE AVAILABLE TO EVERYONE: the study aims to provide A RESOURCE for identifying the region with anatomical criteria THAT ARE EVIDENT USING UBIQUITOUS STAINING METHODS, SUCH AS A NISSL STAIN. A definition is chosen partly for the commonness of the equipment needed to apply it
span.quote: The two major aims of this study were therefore (i) to provide a resource for identifying mouse PPC with anatomical criteria that are evident using ubiquitous staining methods, such as a Nissl stain, and (ii) to define where PPC falls in relation to extrastriate areas around V1.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: WHEN THE ANATOMY OFFERS NO LANDMARKS, FUNCTION IS BORROWED TO SERVE AS ONE: since the dorsal cortical surface in rodents LACKS GROSS ANATOMICAL LANDMARKS, the pattern of responses in the surrounding areas has provided INCREASINGLY-USED FUNCTIONAL LANDMARKS for locating higher visual and associative regions. A location is fixed by what a region DOES because there is nothing to see
span.quote: Since the dorsal cortical surface in rodents lacks gross anatomical landmarks, the pattern of responses in extrastriate areas have provided increasinglyused functional landmarks for locating higher visual (Garrett et al., 2014) and associative regions in the posterior cortex

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AND THE BORROWED METHOD CARRIES ITS OWN PRECONDITION, WHICH IS STATED: functional mapping of that kind is NOT FEASIBLE IN THE ABSENCE OF a broadly expressed calcium indicator or intrinsic optical imaging - so the substitute for the missing definition is itself unavailable to laboratories without those tools
span.quote: However, functional mapping of this kind is not feasible in the absence of a broadly expressed calcium indicator or intrinsic optical imaging, and the location of these areas relative to PPC had not been defined explicitly until now.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE TWO NAMING SYSTEMS ARE FOUND TO OVERLAP PARTIALLY, NOT CLEANLY, AND THE PATTERN IS REPORTED PIECE BY PIECE: the anterior pole of the region DOES NOT OVERLAP with any of the neighbouring areas, the posterior sectors OVERLAP PARTLY with two of them, and its most lateral and posterior extent LARGELY OVERLAPPED with a third. Neither vocabulary's units nest inside the other's
span.quote: we established that the anterior pole of PPC does not overlap with any extrastriate areas, whereas the posterior sectors of PPC overlap partly with areas A and AM. The most lateral and posterior extents of PPC, area PtP (Paxinos & Franklin, 2012), largely overlapped with area RL.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A NAME IS SHOWN TO ASSERT SOMETHING ITS OWN EVIDENCE COMPLICATES: these areas ARE REFERRED TO AS EXTRASTRIATE, IMPLYING A PRIMACY OF VISUAL PROCESSING - THOUGH they OVERLAP CONSIDERABLY with a region the paper characterises as cognitive. The label's morphology makes a claim about what the territory is for, and the overlap is the counter-evidence
span.quote: These areas are referred to as “extrastriate”, implying a primacy of visual processing (Wang & Burkhalter, 2007; Andermann et al., 2011; Marshel et al., 2011; Garrett et al., 2014), though they overlap considerably with PPC, which has cognitive

span.label: Where associative, motor and sensory inputs are integrated synaptically inside PPC, and whether modality-specific topographies exist there, remain unmapped.
span.quote: As for mice, it remains to be mapped more fully where the inputs from associative, motor, and sensory areas are integrated synaptically within PPC, and whether graded topographies exists for different sensory modalities, as shown for visual and vibrissal afferents in area RL (Olcese et al., 2013).

span.label: The mapping was done only against extrastriate visual projections; equivalent mapping against somatosensory, auditory or motor inputs was not performed.
span.quote: While the present study focused on characterizing PPC relative to extrastriate projections, comparable mapping could likely be performed in the context of somatosensory, auditory or motor inputs.

span.label: Antibody cross-reactivity between M2-receptor staining and BDA tracer labelling was observed and had to be controlled for post hoc.
span.quote: Although we noted cross-reactivity between antibodies against M2-receptors and BDA labeling (Figures 3F-G), we confirmed that the patterns of MAChR2 labeling in other sections matched staining patterns in tissue preparations without BDA injections (as in Figure 1).

span.label: Existing targeting strategies are consistent inside a study and incomparable between studies.
span.quote: may yield consistent recording locations within a study, but hamper the comparison of PPC across studies since they are based on different labeling methodologies and unrelated nomenclatures

span.label: The boundaries that distinguish the area from its neighbours are stated to remain ill-defined.
span.quote: including the boundaries which distinguish it from neighboring areas, its laminar organization and chemoarchitectural profile remain ill-defined

span.label: The criteria for defining the area are stated not to have been established before this paper.
span.quote: In this study, we described laminar, cytoarchitectonic and chemoarchitectonic criteria for defining the mouse PPC and surrounding cortices, which, to our knowledge, have not been established previously

span.label: mouse PPC
span.term: mouse PPC
span.quote: We sought to resolve these discrepancies by first delineating mouse PPC using cytoarchitectural and laminar criteria obtained from Nissl-, parvalbumin (PV)-, and type-2 muscarinic acetylcholine receptor (M2AChR)-immunostained coronal sections

span.quote: We sought to resolve these discrepancies by first delineating mouse PPC using cytoarchitectural and laminar criteria obtained from Nissl-, parvalbumin (PV)-, and type-2 muscarinic acetylcholine receptor (M2AChR)-immunostained coronal sections

span.quote: including the boundaries which distinguish it from neighboring areas, its laminar organization and chemoarchitectural profile remain ill-defined

span.label: labeling methodologies
span.term: labeling methodologies
span.quote: may yield consistent recording locations within a study, but hamper the comparison of PPC across studies since they are based on different labeling methodologies and unrelated nomenclatures

span.label: mouse PPC - A REGION IN ROUTINE USE WITHOUT ESTABLISHED CRITERIA: the boundaries distinguishing it from neighbouring areas are said to remain ill-defined, and the criteria this paper supplies are said not to have been established previously, so experiments had been targeting a region whose extent each laboratory fixed for itself
span.quote: including the boundaries which distinguish it from neighboring areas, its laminar organization and chemoarchitectural profile remain ill-defined

span.label: comparability, here - PRESENT WITHIN A STUDY AND ABSENT ACROSS THEM: the same targeting strategies give consistent recording locations inside one study while hampering comparison between studies, because the studies rest on different labeling methodologies and unrelated nomenclatures - so a PPC result is reproducible where it was made and unjoinable elsewhere
span.quote: may yield consistent recording locations within a study, but hamper the comparison of PPC across studies since they are based on different labeling methodologies and unrelated nomenclatures

span.label: the delineation - THREE STAINS AND A LAMINAR READING: PPC is delineated using cytoarchitectural and laminar criteria from Nissl, parvalbumin and M2 muscarinic receptor immunostaining, so the region's extent is defined by what those particular stains show
span.quote: We sought to resolve these discrepancies by first delineating mouse PPC using cytoarchitectural and laminar criteria obtained from Nissl-, parvalbumin (PV)-, and type-2 muscarinic acetylcholine receptor (M2AChR)-immunostained coronal sections

span.label: builds-on → Montero (1993) and Wang & Burkhalter (2007) extrastriate area maps
span.quote: A main goal of this study was to describe the location of extrastriate areas as described by Montero (1993) and Wang & Burkhalter (2007) in relation to the laminar, cyto- and chemoarchitectural features that distinguish PPC in the mouse.

span.label: extends → Wang & Burkhalter (2007), V1 projection mapping
span.quote: By characterizing the architectural boundaries of PPC and cross-referencing them with projections from V1 (Wang & Burkhalter, 2007), we established that the anterior pole of PPC does not overlap with any extrastriate areas, whereas the posterior sectors of PPC overlap partly with areas A and AM.

span.label: replicates → Wang & Burkhalter (2007), topography of V1 projections to LM and AL
span.quote: Also consistent with prior observations (Wang & Burkhalter, 2007), LM showed a mirrored medial-to-lateral ordering of the labeling (Figure 2A), as did the prominently labeled anterolateral (AL) field, just posterior to the S1 barrels.

span.label: mouse PPC —operationalised-as→ cytoarchitectural and laminar criteria
span.term: mouse PPC
cytoarchitectural and laminar criteria
span.quote: We sought to resolve these discrepancies by first delineating mouse PPC using cytoarchitectural and laminar criteria obtained from Nissl-, parvalbumin (PV)-, and type-2 muscarinic acetylcholine receptor (M2AChR)-immunostained coronal sections

span.label: Medial PPC is marked out from its neighbours by a drop in parvalbumin staining in both cell bodies and neuropil, against dense PV staining in adjacent retrosplenial and somatosensory cortex.
span.quote: A salient cellular marker for the appearance of mPPC is the decrease in PV staining in both cell bodies and the neuropil (Figure 1, middle column, row 2), which contrasts with the dense staining medially in layers II-V of RSA, and the darker staining in layers IV and V of S1 (Figure 1, rows 1 and 2).

span.label: A sharp fall in M2 muscarinic acetylcholine receptor staining in superficial layers marks the border between agranular retrosplenial cortex and medial PPC.
span.quote: The border between RSA and mPPC is marked by a sharp decrease in M2AChR staining in the superficial parietal layers, which returns laterally in S1 (Figure 1, right column, row 2).

span.label: Because V2M closely resembles PPC in Nissl and staining terms, the appearance of primary visual cortex is the most reliable sign that a coronal section lies caudal to all PPC subdivisions.
span.quote: Here, the emergence of V1 is marked by strong M2AChR staining directly posterior to lPPC and PtP; again the appearance of V1 is the best indicator of being caudal to all PPC sub-fields in the coronal plane.

span.label: The anterior pole of PPC overlaps no extrastriate area, its posterior sectors overlap areas A and AM, and its most lateral-posterior part PtP overlaps largely with area RL - reconciling the Paxinos-Franklin parietal nomenclature with the Montero/Wang-Burkhalter extrastriate one.
span.quote: we established that the anterior pole of PPC does not overlap with any extrastriate areas, whereas the posterior sectors of PPC overlap partly with areas A and AM. The most lateral and posterior extents of PPC, area PtP (Paxinos & Franklin, 2012), largely overlapped with area RL.

span.label: At -1.91mm from bregma all labelled fibres of extrastriate area A fall inside lateral PPC, with no extrastriate label in medial PPC.
span.quote: As shown in Figure 3B, at -1.91mm posterior to bregma the entire complement of labeled fibers for area A is contained in lPPC, with no apparent extrastriate labeling in mPPC.

span.label: Anterograde injections confined to PPC label the associative thalamic nuclei LP, Po and, more anteriorly, LD.
span.quote: As shown in Figures 4A and B, tracer injections contained wholly within the cytoarchitectonic boundaries of PPC produced robust anterograde labeling in LP and Po, and farther anterior sections contained strong projections confined to LD (Supplementary Figure 1).

span.label: PPC thalamic output was specific to associative nuclei, sparing the adjacent primary relay nuclei DLG (visual) and VPM (somatosensory).
span.quote: In all cases, the thalamic projections were specific to associative nuclei with no staining in the immediately adjacent dorsal lateral geniculate nucleus (DLG), which receives projections from V1, nor in the ventral posterior medial nucleus (VPM), which receives projections from S1.

span.label: Parietal output to frontal cortex is coarsely topographic: medial PPC projects to cingulate cortex and lateral PPC to secondary motor cortex.
span.quote: The injections also produced strong labeling in cingulate (Cg) and secondary motor (M2) cortices, which appeared to follow a coarsely topographical distribution, with medial PPC projecting medially toward Cg, and lateral PPC projecting more laterally into M2 (Figure 5C-D, left).

span.label: Monosynaptic rabies tracing showed PPC receives input from every cortical area to which it sends anterograde label, so all these cortical connections are reciprocal.
span.quote: To determine whether these cortical outputs of PPC were reciprocal, we performed monosynaptic circuit tracing with rabies virus in a parallel series of mice (n = 4, Figure 5A, right) (Wickersham et al., 2007), which yielded unequivocal evidence that PPC received monosynaptic inputs from each cortical area with anterograde labeling (Figure 5B-E, right).

span.label: PPC's densest cortical projections go to extrastriate areas AM/V2M and AL/V2L, with AM/V2M showing a medial-to-lateral topography matching the injection sites and AL/V2L sometimes showing a mirrored order.
span.quote: The densest projections from PPC were to extrastriate areas AM/V2M and AL/V2L (Figure 6B, middle and bottom), with AM/V2M showing a medial-to-lateral topography in line with the location of tracer injections in PPC, and AL/V2L in some cases showing a mirrored ordering

span.label: V1 projects most strongly to the lateromedial field immediately lateral to it and to the laterointermediate field beyond that.
span.quote: Similar to their findings, we report a particularly strong projection from V1 to the lateromedial (LM) field, located immediately lateral to V1, and to the laterointermediate (LI) field lateral to LM (Figure 2A).

span.label: coherent anatomical definition of mouse PPC (laminar architecture, extrastriate projections, thalamic and cortico-cortical connections)
span.term: coherent anatomical definition of mouse PPC (laminar architecture, extrastriate projections, thalamic and cortico-cortical connections)
span.quote: These combined approaches provide a coherent definition of mouse PPC that incorporates laminar architecture, extrastriate projections, thalamic, and cortico-cortical connections.

span.label: flat maps (tangential sections through flattened cortex)
span.term: flat maps (tangential sections through flattened cortex)
span.quote: The left hemisphere was flattened to make “flat maps” of cortex, which first required that cortex was dissected from the rest of the subcortical structures

span.label: site of the triple anterograde tracer injection (V1 versus PPC coordinates)
span.term: site of the triple anterograde tracer injection (V1 versus PPC coordinates)
span.quote: we used coordinates from our prior annotations (Figures 1 and 3) to target triple anterograde tracer injections in PPC (four bilaterally, and two unilaterally), and cut the right hemisphere in coronal sections to investigate the patterns of thalamic labeling.

span.label: pattern and density of anterograde label in cortical and subcortical targets
span.term: pattern and density of anterograde label in cortical and subcortical targets
span.quote: To verify the projection targets of PPC, we next examined labeling resulting from triple-injections in coronal sections of the right hemisphere (Figure 5A, left), which showed prominent labeling in several cortical and sub-cortical regions.

span.label: 24 — total number of adult C57BL/6JBomTac mice used in the study
span.quote: A total number of 24 adult C57BL/6JBomTac mice (24-35 g, Taconic) were used in the current study.

span.label: 600µm — anterior-to-posterior extent of mouse PPC between somatosensory and visual cortices
span.quote: Similar to the rat, the mouse PPC lies between primary somatosensory and visual cortices, spanning approximately 600µm anterior-to-posterior, and has distinguishable medial (mPPC), lateral (lPPC) and posterior (PtP) divisions (Paxinos & Watson, 2013; Olsen & Witter 2017).

span.label: -1.55mm — bregma level at which medial PPC first appears in coronal sections
span.quote: The medial PPC (mPPC) first emerges at approximately -1.55mm relative to bregma, and is apparent by its homogeneous lamination relative to the neighboring agranular retrosplenial cortex (RSA), medially, and S1, laterally.

span.label: -1.91mm — bregma level at which all labelled fibres of extrastriate area A lie within lateral PPC
span.quote: As shown in Figure 3B, at -1.91mm posterior to bregma the entire complement of labeled fibers for area A is contained in lPPC, with no apparent extrastriate labeling in mPPC.

span.label: 0.37mm / 1.25mm / -1.90mm — spacing between the three PPC injections and their starting mediolateral and anteroposterior stereotaxic coordinates
span.quote: The injections into PPC were spaced 0.37mm apart, beginning 1.25mm lateral from of the midline, -1.90mm posterior to bregma.

span.label: 12 days / 230nl / 11 days — interval between helper virus and rabies injection, rabies volume, and survival time before perfusion
span.quote: 12 days later, 230nl of rabies virus (EnvA-pseudotyped SAD-DeltaG-mCherry; gift from Kentros lab) was injected in the same location, and the animal was kept alive for 11 days before perfusion.

span.label: eight / two — number of mice receiving bilateral versus unilateral V1 tracer injections
span.quote: The tracer injections were performed bilaterally in eight mice and unilaterally in two

span.label: n = 4 — number of mice used for monosynaptic rabies retrograde tracing from PPC
span.quote: To determine whether these cortical outputs of PPC were reciprocal, we performed monosynaptic circuit tracing with rabies virus in a parallel series of mice (n = 4, Figure 5A, right) (Wickersham et al., 2007), which yielded unequivocal evidence that PPC received monosynaptic inputs from each cortical area with anterograde labeling (Figure 5B-E, right).

span.label: 40µm — thickness of the coronal sections, cut in three equally spaced series
span.quote: The hemisphere was then cut in 40µm coronal sections on a freezing microtome (see above) in three equally spaced series.
